title: Portal Security: High-Volume Sharing Architecture for 500,000 Users

steps.prompt: An Experience Cloud portal will serve 500,000 Customer Community users who each need read access to their own Cases and sibling account Cases. Which sharing mechanism avoids group maintenance performance degradation?

options.label: Apex Managed Sharing rules recalculating CaseShare records dynamically on user navigation
options.distractorAntipattern: Customer Community (high-volume) licenses do not possess individual share table entries; Apex sharing creates massive calculation overhead.
options.rationale: Customer Community (high-volume) licenses do not support standard share tables (CaseShare); attempting Apex sharing triggers severe table bloat and locking.

options.label: Criteria-Based Sharing Rules targeting Public Groups populated with community user roles
options.distractorAntipattern: High-Volume Customer Community users do not have user roles and cannot be added to Public Groups.
options.rationale: High-Volume Customer Community licenses do not use the standard role hierarchy or public groups, rendering criteria-based sharing rules inapplicable.

options.label: Sharing Sets and Share Groups configured on the portal profile to map account relationships
options.rationale: Sharing Sets grant access based on user account/contact matching without writing to physical share tables, scaling seamlessly to millions of users.
